notes.body:
Model for the hepatic metabolism of losartan.
losartan exchanges fast between the blood of the liver and the hepatocytes (LOSIM)
losartan -> E3174 (CYP2C9, LOS2E3174)
losartan -> other metabolites (LOS2L158, CYP2C9 for the fraction f_l158_cyp2c9, CYP3A4 and UGTs for the rest)
export of E3174 and the other metabolites into the blood and the bile
The concentrations of the liver model are blood concentrations (the species of the whole-body model), the rate constants are intrinsic clearances of blood per liver volume. CYP2C9 forms about 55-60 % of the hepatic clearance: the loss of CYP2C9 (*3/*3, bucolome) increases the AUC of losartan 1.7-2.4 fold and decreases the AUC of E3174 to 0.1-0.2 [Bae2011, Kobayashi2008].
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

body.p: Bile E3174 amount.
Bile other losartan metabolites amount.

Relative activity of CYP2C9: 1.0 normal activity (wildtype), <1.0 reduced activity (genotypes, inhibition), >1.0 increased activity (induction). Set by the experiments (genotype, interactions), not fitted.

parameter.name: fraction of the formation of the other metabolites by CYP2C9

body.p: The oxidative metabolites of losartan (L-158,795/796) are formed by CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, the glucuronides by UGTs. 0.5 gives together with the formation of E3174 a CYP2C9 share of about 0.55 of the hepatic clearance: losartan AUC x2.4 and E3174 AUC x0.12 in CYP2C9 *3/*3 [Bae2011], losartan AUC x1.67 and E3174 AUC x0.165 with bucolome [Kobayashi2008].

First order: the Km of CYP2C9 for losartan (about 1.1 µM unbound [Maekawa2009, Wang2014]) is far above the unbound concentrations (fu 1.3 %), the exposure is dose proportional from 25 to 200 mg [Ohtawa1993]. 14 % of a dose is converted [Lo1995].
The value of LI__LOS2E3174_k is the result of the fit PK_20261019_113633__d9465, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

The hepatic clearance which does not form E3174, about 85 % of the non-renal clearance [Lo1995, FDA1995S60].

Export of E3174 from the hepatocytes into the blood, fitted. It is slow and, with the bile export, sets the retention of the E3174 formed in the hepatocytes, i.e., the delayed appearance of E3174 in plasma (tmax 3-4 hr after intravenous and oral losartan [Lo1995]).
The value of LI__E3174EX_k is the result of the fit PK_20261019_113633__d9465, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

Uptake of E3174 from the blood into the hepatocytes (OATP), concentrative. With the bile export it sets the non-renal clearance of E3174 (21 ml/min of plasma, 45 % of its clearance [Lo1995]).

parameter.name: rate export of the other metabolites

body.p: The non-renal clearance of E3174 is 45 % of its plasma clearance (47 ml/min, renal 26 ml/min [Lo1995]), about 10 % of a dose of losartan is found as E3174 in the feces [FDA1995S60].
The value of LI__E3174BIEX_k is the result of the fit PK_20261019_113633__d9465, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: rate bile export of the other metabolites

body.p: The metabolites of losartan which are not E3174 are recovered in about equal parts in the urine and the feces (17.9 and 17.7 % of an intravenous dose [FDA1995S60]).
The value of LI__L158BIEX_k is the result of the fit PK_20261019_113633__d9465, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

Exchange of losartan between the blood and the hepatocytes, partly by OATP transporters (OATP2B1). Assumption: fast exchange, i.e., the concentration of the hepatocytes is the one of the blood and the hepatic clearance is limited by the metabolism and the blood flow (extraction 0.68 [Lo1995]).
Oxidation of losartan via the aldehyde E3179 to the carboxylic acid E3174, mainly by CYP2C9 (minor CYP3A4).
The inactive metabolites of losartan: the hydroxylated L-158,795 and L-158,796 and L-158,783 (CYP2C9, CYP3A4) and the glucuronides (UGT). They are lumped into one species.
Assumption: fast transport.
